title: Western Australia's low domestic gas prices owe more to abundant, cheap offshore gas and a small market than to reservation
oneLiner: The precedent may show geology, not policy.
body: Western Australia's LNG projects draw on large offshore fields with low production costs, and its domestic market is a fraction of the east coast's. Critics of the comparison argue those conditions would produce low prices with or without a reservation rule, so the policy cannot be credited with the gap.
contextBackground: The causal question behind the WA comparison. It is rarely separated out in public debate, where 'WA has reservation and cheap gas' is treated as settling the matter.
contextDisagreement: Supporters of reservation answer that WA's domestic price has tracked well below what its export-linked price would have been, which is the policy's effect regardless of how cheap the gas is to produce.

evidenceItems.citation: The Conversation, Kevin Morrison, 7 May 2026 — notes compliance with WA's 15 per cent reservation has been poor

otherClaim.title: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's

claimItself.title: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's
claimItself.oneLiner: The one Australian jurisdiction with reservation has had the cheapest domestic gas.
claimItself.body: Since 2006 Western Australia has negotiated a 15 per cent domestic reservation into the approval of each LNG project. Through the east-coast price spikes of 2017 and 2022 its domestic wholesale prices stayed a fraction of eastern levels.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Western Australia's low domestic gas prices owe more to abundant, cheap offshore gas and a small market than to reservation

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim contradicts “Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's”
